subject: general
question: The Chambal, Hindon and Tons rivers are tributaries of the river:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Yamuna**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The significant tributaries of the Yamuna River** include the **Tons, Chambal, Hindon, Betwa, and Ken.**
 
• Originating from the Bhadakla Falls in the Janapav Hills near Mandav, Madhya Pradesh, the Chambal River stretches approximately 1,024 kilometers (636 miles) before joining the Yamuna River in Central and Northern India.
 
• The Hindon River, spanning 400 kilometers in length, serves as another tributary of the Yamuna River. It originates from the Shakumbhari Devi range in the Saharanpur district of Uttar Pradesh, traversing six districts including Saharanpur, Muzaffarnagar, and Meerut.
 
• Flowing through the Garhwal region in Uttarakhand and touching Himachal Pradesh, the Tons River contributes as a tributary to the Yamuna River. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **The Yamuna River, **a prominent waterway in northern India, holds the distinction of being the longest tributary and the second-largest contributor to the Ganges River by discharge.
 
• Stretching across a length of 1,376 kilometers, it encompasses a vast basin area spanning 366,223 square kilometers.
 
• Originating from the Yamunotri glacier nestled in the Himalayan Mountains at an elevation of 6,387 meters, the Yamuna meanders through Yamunanagar before converging at the Triveni Sangam in Prayagraj.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Mahanadi River**, a significant watercourse in East Central India, covers an expansive drainage area of approximately 132,100 square kilometers and spans a total length of 900 kilometers.
 
• Flowing through the states of Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, the **Kaveri River **stands as one of the major rivers in India.
 
• In central India, the **Tapi River** emerges as a notable waterway, coursing from east to west for approximately 724 kilometers.
